daily.title: New Every Morning
daily.text: It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
daily.reflection: Yesterday's failures do not get the last word. God's mercy is not a reserve that runs low; it is renewed with the sunrise. Begin today by receiving it rather than trying to earn it.
daily.prayer: Faithful Lord, thank you for mercies that meet me fresh this morning. Help me walk in them today and extend them to others.

daily.title: Trust Over Understanding
daily.text: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
daily.reflection: Trust is not the absence of thinking but the refusal to make our own understanding the final authority. Where are you leaning hardest on your own read of things today?
daily.prayer: Lord, I bring you the decisions in front of me. Direct my paths where I cannot see the way.

daily.title: The Shepherd's Care
daily.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake.
daily.reflection: Sheep do not provide for themselves; they follow. Rest, restoration and direction all come from staying near the Shepherd.
daily.prayer: Good Shepherd, lead me to rest today and restore what is weary in me.

daily.title: Rest for the Weary
daily.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
daily.reflection: Jesus does not remove every yoke; he offers his own in exchange. Name the burden you have been carrying alone and hand it over.
daily.prayer: Jesus, I come to you tired. Teach me your gentle way and give my soul rest.

daily.title: Be Still
daily.text: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.
daily.reflection: Stillness is an act of faith in a noisy world. Before reading the headlines, take a minute to remember who is exalted over all of them.
daily.prayer: God, quiet my heart. You are God and I am not, and that is good news.

daily.title: Peace Beyond Understanding
daily.text: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
daily.reflection: Paul's cure for anxiety is specific prayer mixed with thanksgiving. Turn each worry today into a request, and pair it with something you are grateful for.
daily.prayer: Father, here are my worries. Guard my heart and mind with your peace.

daily.title: Strength in Waiting
daily.text: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
daily.reflection: Waiting on the Lord is not idleness; it is dependence. Strength is renewed, not manufactured.
daily.prayer: Lord, as I wait on you, renew my strength for what today requires.

daily.title: All Things Together
daily.text: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
daily.reflection: This verse does not say all things are good, but that God weaves all things toward good. Hold your hard circumstances inside that larger story.
daily.prayer: God, I trust you to work even this for good. Help me love you in the middle of it.

daily.title: Do Not Fear
daily.text: Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
daily.reflection: The reason not to fear is not that nothing is frightening but that God is present. His presence is the promise.
daily.prayer: Lord, uphold me today. Replace my fear with confidence in your nearness.

daily.title: Love Defined
daily.text: Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil;
daily.reflection: Read this list with one specific person in mind. Which phrase is hardest to live out toward them today?
daily.prayer: God of love, make me patient and kind, especially with those I find difficult.

daily.title: Lamp and Light
daily.text: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
daily.reflection: A lamp shows the next step, not the whole road. God's Word is often enough light for today's obedience.
daily.prayer: Lord, light my next step through your Word, and give me faith for the rest.

daily.title: A New Creation
daily.text: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
daily.reflection: Your identity in Christ is not a renovation of the old self but a new creation. Live from that identity today.
daily.prayer: Jesus, thank you for making me new. Help me live like who you say I am.

daily.title: Seek First
daily.text: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.
daily.reflection: Priorities shape worry. When the kingdom is first, tomorrow's concerns shrink to their proper size.
daily.prayer: Father, set my priorities in order. Let your kingdom come first in my day.

daily.title: The Fruit of the Spirit
daily.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.
daily.reflection: Fruit grows from connection, not effort alone. Which of these do you most need the Spirit to grow in you this season?
daily.prayer: Holy Spirit, grow your fruit in me, especially where I am lacking.

daily.title: Confident Access
daily.text: Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.
daily.reflection: Because of Jesus our High Priest, we do not approach God timidly. Bring your need boldly.
daily.prayer: Father, I come boldly because of Jesus. I need your grace for this day.

daily.title: Created for Good Works
daily.text: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.
daily.reflection: Good works are not the root of salvation but its fruit. Look for the good work God has prepared for you to walk in today.
daily.prayer: Thank you for saving me by grace. Open my eyes to the good works you have prepared.

daily.title: Confession and Cleansing
daily.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
daily.reflection: Confession is not groveling; it is agreeing with God and receiving his faithful forgiveness. Keep short accounts with him.
daily.prayer: Lord, I confess my sin to you. Thank you for your faithful forgiveness and cleansing.

daily.title: Delight in the Lord
daily.text: Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart. Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass.
daily.reflection: As we delight in God, our desires are reshaped by him. Delight comes before direction.
daily.prayer: Lord, be my delight. Shape the desires of my heart and I commit my way to you.

daily.title: Living Sacrifice
daily.text: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service. And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.
daily.reflection: What we consume shapes our minds. As you read the news today, ask what it means to be transformed rather than conformed.
daily.prayer: God, I offer myself to you today. Renew my mind so I can discern your will.

daily.title: Mercy, Justice, Humility
daily.text: He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?
daily.reflection: Headlines often reveal injustice. Consider one concrete way to do justice or show mercy in your own sphere this week.
daily.prayer: Lord, make me just in my dealings, merciful in my heart, and humble in my walk with you.

daily.title: The Vine and Branches
daily.text: Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me. I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
daily.reflection: Abiding is the work beneath all other work. Fruitfulness flows from staying connected to Christ.
daily.prayer: Jesus, keep me abiding in you. Apart from you I can do nothing.

daily.title: Strong and Courageous
daily.text: Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
daily.reflection: Courage here is a command grounded in a promise: God goes wherever you go today.
daily.prayer: Lord, give me courage for what frightens me today, knowing you are with me.

daily.title: Casting Cares
daily.text: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
daily.reflection: Humility and casting our cares go together: pride insists on carrying everything ourselves.
daily.prayer: Father, I cast my cares on you because you care for me.

daily.title: God So Loved
daily.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.
daily.reflection: God's posture toward the world, the same world in today's news, is love that gives. Let that shape how you see the people in the headlines.
daily.prayer: God, thank you for your saving love. Help me see the world as you do.

daily.title: Wisdom Asked For
daily.text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
daily.reflection: God gives wisdom generously and without scolding. What situation needs his wisdom today?
daily.prayer: Lord, I lack wisdom. Please give it to me generously as you promised.

daily.title: Renewed Inwardly
daily.text: For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day. For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory; While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.
daily.reflection: The news is about what is seen. Faith trains our eyes to also fix on what is unseen and eternal.
daily.prayer: Lord, renew me inwardly today and lift my eyes to what is eternal.

daily.title: Refuge and Strength
daily.text: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be removed, and though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea; Though the waters thereof roar and be troubled, though the mountains shake with the swelling thereof. Selah.
daily.reflection: When the world feels unstable, God remains a very present help. Take refuge in him before reacting to troubling news.
daily.prayer: God, you are my refuge. I will not fear though the world is shaken.

daily.title: Salt and Light
daily.text: Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid. Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
daily.reflection: Light is meant to be seen for the sake of others and for God's glory. Where can your light shine today?
daily.prayer: Father, let my life point others to you today.

daily.title: Nothing Can Separate
daily.text: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
daily.reflection: Paul lists everything imaginable, present and future, and none of it can separate us from God's love. Rest secure in that today.
daily.prayer: Thank you, Lord, that nothing can separate me from your love in Christ.

daily.title: Rejoice Always
daily.text: Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.
daily.reflection: Joy, prayer and thanksgiving are not moods but practices. Try pausing to give thanks at three points in your day.
daily.prayer: Lord, teach me to rejoice, pray and give thanks in every circumstance.

daily.title: The Lord Bless You
daily.text: The LORD bless thee, and keep thee: The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee: The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.
daily.reflection: End the month under God's blessing. Receive it, then speak it over someone you love.
daily.prayer: Lord, bless and keep me and those I love. Make your face shine upon us and give us peace.

weekly.practice: Pray the Lord's Prayer slowly each morning this week, pausing on each line.
questions: When did prayer feel most real this week?
What did I ask God for, and what did I hear?

weekly.practice: Write down three specific things you are thankful for each day.
questions: What gifts did I overlook this week?
How did gratitude change my outlook?

weekly.practice: Set aside a screen-free block of time to rest and worship.
questions: What robbed me of rest this week?
What truly restores me?

weekly.practice: Give something (time, money or attention) anonymously this week.
questions: Where was I tight-fisted?
How did giving affect my heart?

weekly.practice: Bring one unresolved grievance to God in prayer every day this week.
questions: Is there anyone I am still holding a debt against?
How have I experienced God's forgiveness?

weekly.practice: Invite someone to share a meal or coffee with you.
questions: Who in my life feels like an outsider?
How did I make room for others this week?

weekly.practice: Look for one chance each day to put someone else's interests first.
questions: Where did pride show up this week?
How is Jesus' humility a model for me?

weekly.practice: Pray daily for one situation of injustice you read about in the news.
questions: Which story this week stirred my compassion?
What is one concrete response I can make?

weekly.practice: Fast from one form of shopping or comparison (ads, social media) this week.
questions: What did I feel I lacked this week?
Where did I find sufficiency in Christ?

weekly.practice: Memorize one verse this week and repeat it at every meal.
questions: Which verse stuck with me?
How did it shape my reactions?

weekly.practice: Before speaking in a tense moment, pause and pray a one-line prayer.
questions: Where did my words build up or tear down?
What conversations need repair?

weekly.practice: Each evening, name one sign of God's faithfulness from the day.
questions: What news threatened my hope this week?
What anchors my hope beyond circumstances?

weekly.practice: Pray by name for three people who do not yet know Jesus.
questions: Where did I have an opportunity to share my faith?
What holds me back?

monthly.focus: Starting the year rooted in God's renewing grace, setting rhythms of Scripture and prayer.
review: What habits of grace do I want to establish this year?
What do I need to leave behind?

monthly.focus: Receiving God's love and learning to love others the way he loves us.
review: Who did I love well this month?
Where did I withhold love?

monthly.focus: Honest self-examination, confession and the joy of restoration.
review: What sin has God brought to light?
Where have I seen renewal?

monthly.focus: Living in the power and hope of Christ's resurrection.
review: What feels dead that I need to entrust to God?
How does the resurrection change my outlook?

monthly.focus: Deepening the practice of prayer: adoration, confession, thanksgiving, supplication.
review: How has my prayer life grown?
What prayers has God answered?

monthly.focus: Walking in step with the Spirit and bearing his fruit.
review: Where have I sensed the Spirit's leading?
Which fruit is growing, and which is lacking?

monthly.focus: Building sustainable rhythms of work, rest and worship.
review: Was my pace sustainable this month?
What adjustments do I need to make?

monthly.focus: Seeking God's wisdom for everyday decisions and a discerning view of the world.
review: What decisions did I bring to God?
How did I respond to the news with wisdom?

monthly.focus: Investing in the church and in relationships that spur one another on.
review: Who encouraged me this month?
Whom did I encourage?

monthly.focus: Remembering God's faithfulness and growing in faithfulness ourselves.
review: Where have I seen God's faithfulness this month?
Where do I need to be more faithful?

monthly.focus: Cultivating a thankful heart in every circumstance.
review: What am I most grateful for this month?
How did thankfulness change my attitude?

monthly.focus: Preparing through Advent to celebrate God with us.
review: How did I make room for Christ this season?
What am I carrying into the new year?
